title: Unloved Chinese Stocks - Value, Buy for 2X?
creator: Sven Carlin
summary: Sven Carlin works through the ~20 largest holdings of the China internet ETF - unloved after 13 years with no performance - screening for value: low P/Es, high cash flows, profitability and growth. Tencent (P/E ~15, dividends, buybacks, double-digit growth) is "interesting" on his buy-the-bad-mood/sell-the-exuberance framework; he owns Prosus as his Tencent proxy. JD.com he owns outright - the investment/profitability cycle swings 50-70%, with very high cash flow per share, dividend, 3.7% buyback yield and a logistics moat. Kuaishou is his standout free bet: core business at P/E ~7 with 68% ownership of Kling AI (raised ~$3B, growing 200%). Baidu trades near book value of its cash with AI/robotaxi optionality; Trip.com at P/E 10 with ~RMB 14B cash looks interesting; Tencent Music is cheap and profitable. Alibaba is "too high now" on declining legacy cash flows; NetEase and Lenovo are fairly priced holds. He avoids KE Holdings (P/E 26, frozen transaction market), Bilibili, GDS and Kingsoft Cloud. Overall: buy big-cap Chinese internet on weakness for ~50% minimum over three years, hold via ETF or directly, size ~10-15% of a global value portfolio - and only for European investors; he explicitly warns US investors off due to sanction/illiquidity risk (VIE structure, Taiwan). Note: auto-captions garble several names (Meituan as "Mu1", Kling AI as "Cling AI", renminbi as "raimi/remimi") - treat P/E and cash figures as approximate.

calls.thesis: P/E ~15 with dividends + buybacks and double-digit growth; his framework: buy on bad mood / sentiment lows, sell into exuberance peaks. He owns Prosus (Tencent proxy) instead of Tencent directly.
